relations.note: The poem names Mímr’s sons but gives neither their number nor identities.

relations.myth: Óðinn’s eye pledged in Mímir’s well
relations.note: Mímir drinks mead from the well containing Óðinn’s pledged eye.

relations.myth: Óðinn purchases wisdom with his eye
relations.note: Mímir grants Óðinn a drink only after Óðinn pledges an eye.

relations.myth: Consultation with Mímr’s head at Ragnarǫk
relations.note: Óðinn consults Mímr’s speaking head as the cosmic crisis begins.
Mímr’s head speaks wise words and true staves associated with runic lore.

relations.myth: Preservation and reanimation of Mímir’s head
relations.note: Óðinn preserves Mímir’s severed head with herbs and spells, restoring speech.

relations.myth: The preserved head reports other worlds
relations.note: Mímir’s head tells Óðinn hidden news from other worlds.
Mímir counsels Óðinn and his following before Ragnarǫk.
Mímir serves as Hœnir’s counsellor and supplies judgments he cannot make alone.
The Vanir accuse the Æsir of fraud, behead Mímir, and return his head.
The two wisest hostages travel in opposite directions without a narrated meeting.
Njǫrðr and Mímir travel on opposing sides of the hostage exchange.
Freyr and Mímir travel on opposing sides of the hostage exchange.
Heimdallr sounds Gjallarhorn while Óðinn consults Mímr’s head; they do not interact.
The heroic Mímir is Sigurðr’s smith-master or foster-father; identity with Eddic Mímir is disputed.
Reginn is the heroic smith Mímir’s brother; identity with Eddic Mímir is disputed.

relations.myth: Mimir and Balder consult the Norns
relations.note: Mímir and Baldr jointly consult the Norns in a Romantic invented scene.

relations.myth: Mimir and Balder consult the Norns
relations.note: Mímir seeks knowledge from the Norns in a Romantic scene absent from medieval myth.
Marvel reinvented Mimir within Thor’s superhero cosmology.

relations.myth: Odin imprisons Mimir in a tree
relations.note: The game’s Odin imprisons and torments Mimir instead of seeking his counsel.
At Mimir’s request, Kratos decapitates him and later carries his reanimated head.
Freya magically reanimates Mimir after Kratos decapitates him.
